transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:54 UTC (54 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Aisha Khan (Starlark, Head of AI), Tom Rivers (Starlark, Infra Lead), Diego Marquez (Starlark SRE), Lena Ortiz (Starlark Procurement), Samir Patel (Starlark Product)

Summary: Quick renewal check-in focused on capacity uplift and adding EU private/private-edge region. Discussed tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, security artifacts (SOC2/SAML/KMS), timeline for EU pilot, and pricing delta for committed capacity. Agreed on technical deep-dive and delivery of committed pricing table.

Topics: committed capacity levels; EU region private deployment; latency targets and KV cache behavior; RBAC and KMS integration; procurement timeline; benchmarks for token throughput; fallback policies and rollouts.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 55 minutes on the calendar, so we'll start. Quick intro — Jordan from Redwood, AE. Priya SE — Priya, wanna say hi?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hey, hi. Priya here, focusing on private deployments and perf. Hey all.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: Hi, Aisha from Starlark. Thanks for squeezing us in; we've got Tom, Diego, Lena and Samir on.
[00:18] Tom Rivers: Morning everyone.
[00:19] Diego Marquez: Hey.
[00:21] Jordan Ellis: Great. Purpose today is to check on renewal cadence — your contract's up in February — and the EU uplift pilot we talked about. We want to capture any blockers and next steps. Marcus is on to help with CSM items. Marcus?
[00:32] Marcus Lee: Hi all, quick note: we're aiming to keep your latency SLOs intact while ramping capacity, and to make procurement easy. I'll own the follow-ups on contracts.
[00:40] Samir Patel: Quick thing — product wants predictable tail-latency, we've seen variability in the q1 trial and want to lock that down before committing to multi-region.
[00:49] Priya Nair: Got it. On variability — a lot depends on continuous batching and KV cache warmup. When you add EU traffic we can pre-warm KV cache and pin model variants to reduce cold starts.
[01:02] Aisha Khan: And on security — procurement wants SOC2 details, also SAML/SSO support and KMS for key management. Is all that baked into the private offering?
[01:12] Jordan Ellis: Yes — private deployment supports SAML/SSO, we integrate with customer KMS and HSM options. We'll share the SOC2 package and the security checklist. There might be a short lead if you want HSM-backed keys in your on-prem instance but we can scope that.
[01:28] Lena Ortiz: From procurement, timeline question: when would you need a signed PO to make the EU pilot in Jan? We have internal cycles.
[01:35] Jordan Ellis: For a January pilot, we'd want a PO by end of December ideally to reserve capacity and schedule infra. But we can be flexible — Marcus can coordinate.
[01:43] Marcus Lee: I'll coordinate. If you commit to the reserved tier, we can bump you into priority staging week of Jan 4th.
[01:51] Tom Rivers: On the technical side, what does network egress look like for private? Do we set up VPC peering or transit gateway? Diego, do you wanna jump in?
[01:59] Diego Marquez: We have tight egress rules and some legacy NATs; need to validate whether Redwood needs a VPN or we can do private endpoints.
[02:06] Priya Nair: For Redwood Private we support VPC peering and dedicated private endpoints. If you prefer, we can also do an on-prem package with appliance-style connectivity; depends on latency and egress requirements.
[02:17] Tom Rivers: Any pinch on throughput for large embedding jobs? We're running batch jobs overnight that create embeddings and we don't want them to disrupt daytime generator traffic.
[02:26] Priya Nair: We recommend separation of pools — dedicated capacity for embeddings batch windows vs real-time generation. We can size the GPU pool and set auto-scale/burst policies to avoid noisy neighbors. The committed capacity tiers outline how many GPUs and expected tokens per second.
[02:42] Aisha Khan: Can you send the exact mapping — like if we pick X tokens per second what GPUs and cost we get? Our CFO needs line items.
[02:50] Jordan Ellis: Absolutely. We'll send a committed capacity matrix with example token math and a sample invoice. Action item there.
[02:57] Samir Patel: On regional routing — do you have automatic failover to hosted region if EU capacity is saturated? We don't want user impact if the private EU cluster is degraded.
[03:08] Priya Nair: Yes, smart routing can failover to a pinned hosted variant or to a lower-precision quantized model if set in policy. We'll show the rollback policies in the deep-dive. There is a small latency impact during failover.
[03:19] Diego Marquez: How about data residency — logs and traces — can we keep those in EU only?
[03:24] Jordan Ellis: For Private we can keep audit logs and tracing within your VPC or region; hosted telemetry can be disabled or scrubbed. We'll include details in the SOC2/architecture note.
[03:35] Lena Ortiz: Procurement needs to know support SLAs. What uptime can we expect and how are credits handled?
[03:41] Marcus Lee: Dedicated and Private have SLA commitments — 99.9% for Dedicated, private SLAs can be part of contract; credits and response times depend on severity. I'll attach the SLA doc to the follow-up.
[03:52] Aisha Khan: Competitor question — we've had a vendor proposing a managed endpoint that claims lower cost on paper using smaller shard sizes. How does Redwood compare on unit economics?
[04:02] Jordan Ellis: We focus on cost controls via batching, caching and quantization profiles. Often the competitor metric looks cheaper but they don't account for KV cache cold-starts or peak tail-latency. We'll include a cost comparison spreadsheet showing real-world token costs across workloads.
[04:18] Samir Patel: For the EU pilot, what's a realistic throughput target for day 1? We're thinking 400 qps for inference and nightly 100k embeddings.
[04:27] Priya Nair: 400 qps is doable with a small dedicated pool if you accept 95th percentile latency under your SLO; embedding pipelines can be scheduled. We'll size and propose a couple of tiers.
[04:38] Tom Rivers: Any upfront engineering work from our side? We want to understand the integration points so we can book SRE time.
[04:45] Priya Nair: We'll need network setup (VPC peering or PrivateLink), SAML metadata for SSO, and KMS details if using your key management. We will provide Terraform snippets and runbook.
[04:56] Diego Marquez: Can you run a small benchmark for our model — custom finetune — to check token throughput?
[05:02] Priya Nair: Yes. If you can share a small model artifact and representative prompts, we can run a pilot benchmark. We'll need a non-prod dataset and an NDA-permitted sample.
[05:13] Lena Ortiz: Procurement follow-up: what is the minimum commitment? We are debating a six-month versus 12-month commit.
[05:20] Jordan Ellis: Minimums depend on the tier; 6-month is possible with a smaller discount. 12-month committed capacity gives better rates and priority staging. We'll show both scenarios in the quote.
[05:31] Marcus Lee: Recap — Jordan will send pricing and example invoice; Priya will schedule deep-dive and runbook; Tom/Diego to send traffic profiles and VPC diagram; Lena will start PO approvals. Marcus will attach SLA and SOC2.
[05:46] Aisha Khan: That all sounds good. Can we aim to have the pricing and security pack by 2026-12-16 so we can decide before holidays?
[05:55] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we can do that. 
[05:57] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, everyone.
[05:58] Jordan Ellis: Thanks. We'll follow up in writing with action items.

End of meeting.
